# Damage sharing, prevention and interception

**REVIEWED / reference-VALIDATED —39 exact source passages and two supporting Tinker engine passages.** [Final notebook review](../../../../docs/audit/2026-10-08/full-game/GPT_REDIRECTION_FINAL_CLOSURE.md) closes this bounded damage-sharing interface with94 checks and186 conservation states. It does not establish every item/spell defense, companion lifecycle, all-source attack chain or numerical balance. Original source cards remain unchanged.

Read the [source register](REDIRECTION_SOURCE_BINDINGS.md), [source checks](REDIRECTION_SOURCE_VALIDATION.json), [reference checks](REDIRECTION_PLAYTEST_VALIDATION.json), [first notebook proposal](../../../../docs/audit/2026-10-08/full-game/GPT_REDIRECTION_FIRST_REVIEW_PARTIAL.md) and [complete corrections](../../../../docs/audit/2026-10-08/full-game/GPT_REDIRECTION_BOUNDARIES.md). Later corrections supersede the retained first proposal.

## Resolve the kind of protection first

Guardian Pulse changes the target of an attack before comparing its original roll with AC. The Guardian becomes the actual hit/miss and on-hit-rider target. One attack can be retargeted once. Multiple offers are chosen by the original intended target; only the selected Guardian spends its Reaction/use. After the incoming attack fully resolves, a surviving, eligible Guardian may make the printed counterattack against an attacker in reach whether the original attack hit or missed. This free attack cannot grant another free attack or Action. Retargeting does not spend the later damage-transfer opportunity.

Bloodbond and Veinlock Tether divide the finalized raw damage before either recipient's mitigation. Attack/save success, save-halving and critical dice have already determined that amount. Bloodbond transfers one quarter, rounded down; Veinlock instead chooses up to S+M. Each recipient applies its own eligible defenses once to its own share.

Other supplied damage transfers divide damage after the original target's defenses and legal pure prevention, before temporary HP. Their transferred portions keep damage type and skip another DR/resistance/immunity/prevention stage. Temporary HP, applicable HP floors, would-die replacements, Wounds, concentration and ordinary life consequences still apply. “Unmitigated damage” does not mean “death cannot be prevented.”

Pure prevention removes damage without creating a second recipient. Elemental Absorption adds its resistance during ordinary defenses. Aura of Bonds and Crown reductions use the strongest applicable class flat reduction, then resistance/immunity. Finite/reactive prevention such as Bloom and Ancestral Guardian follows those defenses before post-defense transfer and temporary HP. Verify additional item/spell sources before treating this as universal defense ordering.

Redirecting Palm prevents half the Monk's post-defense damage, rounded down. The Monk keeps the remainder. A second enemy distinct from the triggering melee attacker, within5feet, can receive new force damage equal to the prevented amount, capped at Monk level. That new damage gets its own defenses; it is not a transferred attack or critical hit. With no second enemy, the Monk still receives the reduction.

Direct HP payments from Blood Sacrifice, Flesh-to-RP, Profane Exchange and Channel Life stay outside the damage sequence. They bypass temporary HP, obey their own legal minimum HP and do not create damage/Wound/resource triggers from paying the cost. Healing-recipient substitution and excess-healing conversion also remain distinct operations.

## One transfer operation and exact amounts

A root here means one original recipient's damage packet. A shared area cast has a separate root for each original recipient, under the same cast/roll identity.

One such root accepts one damage-sharing operation across all owners. A pre-mitigation split locks both its retained original portion and transferred portions against later transfer. Burden Shared can divide one operation among up to two other explicitly willing recipients. It does not create two redirection events. No transferred recipient may be the original damage target.

**New stage-precedence integration:** consider pre-mitigation offers before applying defenses, and post-defense offers afterward. Within the same stage, select eligible positive mandatory/automatic protection before optional offers; competing mandatory claims are chosen by the original damage target. A legally chosen Bloodbond/Veinlock operation can therefore preempt later Aegis/Final Stand because that root is already claimed. Do not preview or consume defenses/Bloom to decide a later-stage preference. The helper accepts an already selected legal operation; it does not select Reactions or schedule automatic offers.

Optional transfer requires a positive chosen amount and available damage. Zero transfer cannot spend an optional Reaction/resource/use. A mandatory rounded-zero share does nothing and spends no transfer allowance. An independently legal prevention component can still occur.

| Source | Transferred amount |
|---|---|
| Bloodbond | floor(raw damage/4), fixed |
| Veinlock Tether / Shared Breath / Selfless Guardian | chosen up to S+M |
| Protective Stance / Emergency Protocols | min(S+M, available damage), fixed |
| Life Linked | chosen up to floor(available damage/2) |
| Guardian Tissue | floor(available damage/3), fixed |
| Aegis Incarnate / Martyr's Share | floor(available damage/2), fixed |
| Chainbound Smite | chosen up to max(3, actual CHA modifier) |
| Linked Ward | chosen up to max(2, twice actual CHA modifier) |
| King's Smite protection | chosen up to5 |
| Aura of the Crown | chosen up to M |
| Crown of Embers / Burden Shared | chosen up to level+M |
| Crown Undying | chosen up to remaining level+M round allowance |
| Final Stand | all available damage, subject to shared allowance |

Every amount is capped by the available packet at its source's stage. Fixed fractions/fixed protection cannot voluntarily choose a smaller amount. Original actions, range, willingness, costs, active-state requirements, cadence and source-specific use limits still apply.

## Hit identity and final damage accounting

The original damage target retains its original hit, failed-save, critical and on-hit-rider identity even if all damage is transferred. A rider that requires positive damage must recheck the actual remaining packet. A transferred recipient was not hit by that attack and did not fail its save; it receives no attached poison/control/maiming/knockout rider merely because damage moved.

Accordingly, transferred damage from a critical attack gives an already0HP recipient the ordinary one damage failure, not two critical-hit failures. Concentration still sees the transferred recipient's resolved packet even if temporary HP absorbs all of it.

Use the [reviewed life-state interface](HEALING_DEATH_PLAYTEST.md) after resolving each final recipient. Numeric actual damage is temporary HP absorbed plus actual normal HP lost, excluding overkill and damage prevented by an HP floor. Sum each terminal recipient once. Do not also count the unsplit parent or unrelated counterdamage.

Physical root totals include every recipient. A healing/resource/reflection consumer sums only branches permitted for that consumer and qualifying for its own source's target predicate. For example, a meaningful-hostile-only drain does not automatically count damage transferred onto a friendly protector. Check all applicable flags for a compound trigger, such as a passive healing proc.

## Source-specific restrictions

All transfers prohibit another transfer. All supplied post-defense transfers prohibit another mitigation/prevention stage. Further restrictions differ:

| Source family | Additional restrictions on transferred damage |
|---|---|
| Paladin engine | No reflection or resource generation; does not universally prohibit other retaliation or healing |
| Protective Stance | Also no generic damage-trigger chains |
| Burden Shared | Also no derived healing |
| Oracle Life Linked | No reflection, resource/RC, passive, condition, action or copy generation; no recovery or retaliation |
| Guardian Tissue / Aegis | No BT generation; no invented ban on every other resource |
| Shared Breath | No additional generic trigger prohibition |
| Selfless Guardian / Emergency Protocols | No retaliation chain |
| Bloodbond / Veinlock | Each recipient still has its one defense stage; no additional blanket prohibition |

A no-derived-healing flag does not prevent unrelated later healing of the recipient.

The source's explicit redirection riders remain narrowly available. Unbroken Covenant triggers on the redirection operation, even when Protective Stance prohibits generic damage triggers; use half the final protector actual damage, capped at S+M. These self-absorption riders require damage actually transferred to the redirecting owner, not to another ally under Burden Shared. Linked Ward's own transfer granting temporary HP on reducing the Paladin to0 uses final actual damage, capped at level+M. Final Stand also gives the protected ally temporary HP equal to Paladin level and resistance to all damage through that ally's next turn end; the numeric helper handles only temporary HP, and the caller must create the resistance record. None grants a generic permission to ignore other source restrictions. Temporary HP still uses the larger remaining amount and does not stack.

## Paladin round ledger

Track each Paladin owner's numbered-round events. Ordinarily, one redirection event is available, using exactly one Paladin redirection feature. Final Stand is automatic on the first eligible positive post-defense packet while its allowance remains; the Paladin cannot save it for a later hit. Its “all damage” text does not override the explicit engine ceiling. It may redirect again in a later numbered round if still active before its source-next-start deadline.

Crown Undying can raise the owner's total to two different damage events, with at most one ordinary/non-Crown feature. The additional permission belongs to Crown Undying. A prior ordinary redirection remains recorded if Crown activates later in the same round; only one further Crown event is then possible. Reapplication does not clear history.

The two Crown events may protect the same selected ally. Sum Crown-transferred amounts against level+M per round. Its heal is floor(final Paladin branch actual damage/2) for each event, then capped by the remaining S+M per protected ally that round. Commit that nominal source entitlement before target healing restrictions; blocked or capped healing refunds no event, transfer amount or healing entitlement. The heal cannot heal the Paladin or start another redirection/heal-copy chain.

## Bloom and devices

Bloom Ward is a finite10+Oracle-level prevention pool across packets. Apply its legal prevention after ordinary defenses. Subtract only the prevented amount. The bloom ends on depletion, its1minute expiry, or actual legal removal. Suppression alone does not end it. Ending grants the printed +1 Frightened-save rider through the target's next end. A late clock observation must retain the endpoint calculated from the actual expiry, not create a fresh duration. An unmitigated transferred branch cannot consume this prevention pool.

Emergency Protocols requires an active/conscious drone within its printed range. The transfer occurs after the Tinker's defenses and before temporary HP. The drone receives the bounded transferred amount without mitigation; legally granted temporary HP can absorb it. At0HP the drone is destroyed and receives no organic Wound or death-save procedure.

Tinker engine[2] retains the destroyed drone at0 until its explicit repair/rebuild procedure. Ordinary functional repair cannot reconstruct a destroyed drone or reset ammunition, uses, duration or command budget. This package's device helper only resolves damage/destruction; it does not implement reconstruction or grant a destruction reward. The broader companion/device lifecycle remains open.

## Reference boundary

The helper validates arithmetic, stages, branch identity, replay protection and round entitlements. Callers establish legal sources, target relationships, exact source cadence, action/resource payment, clock endpoints and source-native riders. No helper imports card ownership merely from a string identifier. The source register preserves every exact original procedure alongside the overlay.

Guardian Pulse's new counterattack carries its explicit no-further-free-attack/no-Action limits, without inheriting unrelated incoming healing/resource/reflection restrictions. Palm's force damage has no invented copy/action/resource prohibition; each downstream source determines eligibility. It cannot trigger another Palm because it is not a melee attack.

Validation currently covers94 targeted checks and186 conservation states. Full-game completion, human balance and all-source combat/device execution remain separate unfinished work.

It does not promote that older table into the approved Core book.

Use [source bindings](../../data/playtest/strain_bindings.json), [source validation](STRAIN_SOURCE_VALIDATION.json), [combat timing](COMBAT_ACTION_PLAYTEST.md), [conditions](CONDITIONS_PLAYTEST.md) and [HP/Wounds](CORE_RESOLUTION_PLAYTEST.md). The [first GPT review](../../../../docs/audit/2026-10-08/full-game/GPT_STRAIN_FIRST_REVIEW.md) and [counterexample corrections](../../../../docs/audit/2026-10-08/full-game/GPT_STRAIN_COUNTEREXAMPLE_REVIEW.md) preserve the decisions. The latter corrects an earlier summary that misplaced the expedition attack/save penalties at level3; their source places them at level2.

## Identify the track first

| Mechanical ID | What it represents | Range | Generic recovery |
|---|---|---:|---|
| `warrior.serum-strain` | The Warrior serum/mutation engine, including an explicit Serum Sharing recipient | 0–3 | Beneficial completed1h Short Rest−1; beneficial completed8h Long Rest→0 |
| `expedition.strain` | Campaign attrition, Rest Debt, unsupported Supply, Quickglass crash and ordinary Wound-treatment critical failure | 0–6 | Secure beneficial Long Rest−1 eligible point; Morale Rest−1; qualifying Haven care removes all eligible ordinary points |

Neither is global `core.exhaustion`, Oracle Revelation backlash, Dissonance or historical Resonance Burn. A single cause applies multiple tracks only if its operative source explicitly says so. Serum3 never becomes expedition3, and serum overflow never becomes expedition6. A namespace binding identifies a reference; it does not itself apply any effect.

Inside the supplied Warrior engine/cards, Strain means serum Strain. In the supplied campaign references, Strain means expedition Strain. **Future ambiguous sources remain unbound until reviewed.** The source register records8 Warrior engine references,17 cards,3 campaign sections and12 exact Core paragraphs. Do not classify a new immunity or source by its name alone.

Quickglass's crash adds1 expedition point and retains its independent one-hour DEX-check disadvantage. Ordinary Wound-treatment Critical Failure adds1 expedition point to the **patient**, without inventing another Wound or Exhaustion level. Morale Rest removes expedition Strain only. Serum Tolerance suppresses the profile side effects it names; it does not prevent serum Strain or its penalties.

## Warrior serum Strain

Preserve the source engine: normal Serum Injection/Mutagen Injection and Mutation Surge add1; Serum Cocktail/Mutation Overload add2 unless a printed modifier applies. Cap3. At2, Speed−5. At3, also AC−1 and saves−1; the source's voluntary serum/Cocktail/Overclock/Surge activation lock applies. All card costs, prepared doses, mutation limits and frequencies remain required.

For an activation explicitly illegal if it exceeds the cap, calculate its **final modified gain first**, including applicable Mutation Adaptation and the minimum1 for Cocktail/Overload where applicable. Reject a resulting value above3. Never clip a voluntary overcap cost into legality. A separate activation lock can still prohibit activation even if a gain modifier makes its cost small or zero.

Automatic later gains, such as the actual **Sanguine Surge** profile's ending side effect, clamp at3. They do not retroactively invalidate the original activation, cause overflow death or add expedition points.

**Serum Sharing — NEW integration.** Its willing recipient receives serum Strain even when not a Warrior. At recipient3, the attempted+1 clamps at3; this is not the recipient activating an otherwise locked class ability. The recipient retains all existing penalties and receives only the card's actual diluted effects and side effects. Source-owner Serum Tolerance does not protect the ally. Recipient Strain uses the same beneficial1h/8h recovery; no serum preparation, mutation slots or other Warrior powers are granted.

## Expedition Strain

NEW interpretation: rows are cumulative. Preserve the original placement of effects:

| Level | Additional consequence |
|---:|---|
| 0 | None |
| 1 | −1 initiative and expedition checks |
| 2 | Speed−10; −1 attacks and saving throws |
| 3 | Disadvantage on expedition checks; Dash lock below |
| 4 | Effective maximum HP×3/4 |
| 5 | Core Incapacitated plus the explicit movement restriction below |
| 6 | Deterministic death/collapse endpoint below |

Initiative−1 applies when a roll is made. Changing Strain does not reorder an established encounter. Ordinary advantage/disadvantage does not numerically stack from multiple sources.

Represent each point with `pointId`, `sourceId`, `ordinaryRemovable` and `removalGateMet`. Level is the active count, maximum6. Keep source history and attempted overflow even when no additional point can be stored. A generic recovery can select only points that are ordinary-removable **and** whose gate is met. A specific treatment can override only the source it expressly covers. Clearing a gate updates metadata; it does not silently delete a point.

**Level6 — NEW deterministic interpretation.** On every positive, unprevented expedition gain that would reach **or exceed6**, evaluate that gain's endpoint before clamping stored points at6. Default: ordinary Dead state. Only that gain's explicit reviewed nonlethal source can instead produce `expedition.collapse`. A living collapsed creature already at6 can die from a later ordinary gain; it is not protected by the cap. A prevented/zero gain causes no endpoint. Nonlethal gains or Strain removal never revive a corpse.

Collapse leaves the creature alive, Unconscious, Speed0 and unable to act/travel. It does not set HP0, grant Stable or create death saves by itself. Independently dying0HP creatures still follow their normal saves. Short/Long/Morale Rest cannot reduce expedition points while this level6 collapse persists; qualifying24h Haven care or explicit treatment may. Collapse ends only when the track falls below6. Other Unconscious sources remain independent. If all six points stay blocked, Haven care cannot clear the collapse by assertion.

This recoverable collapse is a **NEW operational replacement** for the source's undefined “permanent collapse” alternative. The original wording remains preserved; it did not itself specify this recovery. Actual resurrection while six expedition points remain is a separate unresolved resurrection interface.

## Independent penalties and maximum HP

Apply flat Speed changes first, floor at0, then applicable multipliers and floor normally. A rule setting Speed0 takes precedence. Serum2's−5 and expedition2's−10 coexist: base30 becomes15, then Exhaustion2's half Speed gives7. Mutation Adaptation's explicit serum Speed exception does not cancel expedition Speed loss.

Expedition2 and serum3 each impose saves−1, totaling−2. The class rule against stacking duplicate bonuses does not merge these independent tracks.

NEW maximum-HP composition: multiply applicable rational factors against the same otherwise-applicable maximum, floor **once**, minimum1. Expedition4×3/4 and Exhaustion4×1/2 produce37 from base100. Clamp currentHP down if necessary; that clamp is not damage and triggers no Wound, death-save failure or damage resource. Removing a modifier raises capacity without healing/resetting death counters. Critical Wounds' healing ceiling then uses `max(1, effectiveMaximumHP−1)`; it is not another maxHP multiplier.

The helper accepts other multipliers only after their compatibility has been established elsewhere. It does not decide whether unrelated gear/ancestry/spell modifiers stack.

## Dash lock — NEW

At expedition3–4, a legal Dash consumes the current opportunity and creates a lock. No other Dash is legal while locked, whether Action, Bonus Action, extra Action or extra turn. A non-Dash Action, round boundary or extra turn does not clear it.

In initiative, lock through the **end of the next future regular turn** of the creature. A Dash during its current turn excludes that current end, using the exact marker-exclusion rule from combat. Thus turn1 Dash blocks another that turn and turn2; turn2's end unlocks turn3. An off-turn Dash locks through the next regular turn's end. Extra turns cannot substitute for that marker.

Outside initiative, unlock at Dash time+6 seconds. Preserve whichever endpoint was recorded across initiative entry/exit/reorder; do not restart or convert it. Falling below expedition3 clears the restriction and stored lock immediately. Returning to3 begins unlocked until a new legal Dash. Expedition5 cannot Dash at all.

The exact review confirms exclusion of the current in-progress turn end. Its earlier “strictly after Dash” shorthand is superseded by these specific marker rules and tests.

## Expedition5 and assistance

Core Incapacitated denies Action/Bonus Action/Reaction and ends concentration. NEW expedition-specific restriction: no voluntary tactical movement in initiative. This does **not** redefine generic Incapacitated or automatically set the creature's actual Speed statistic to0. Forced movement, an external legal teleport and lawful carrying still work.

Outside combat, apply the slow-travel exception by halving the otherwise legal walking/travel pace once after applicable load/Speed/environment rules. Do not repeatedly halve per Watch or invent miles-per-hour values here. Detailed stacking with other travel-pace modifiers remains the travel review's responsibility.

Brief communication is possible if no other condition prevents it. The victim cannot use an Action-time consumable by itself. A legal willing recipient can be fed, given a potion or treated by someone paying the actual required Action/activity, supplies and costs. This creates no free administration or universal restraint/capture rule. Rest and Haven care remain possible when their eligibility requirements are met.

## Recovery and actual elapsed time

Preserve campaign limits: Short Rest1h, at most **two beneficial Short Rests between beneficial Long Rests**; Long Rest8h, at most **one beneficial Long Rest per24 elapsed hours**. Those limits apply to serum recovery too, including non-Warrior recipients. Exact completion timestamps and IDs prevent replay. Work, travel, short rest, sleep and recreation cannot spend the same active hours twice. Unfinished/interrupted activity provides no completion benefit.

**Rest Debt order.** First complete a qualifying safe8hRestWatch and clear debt it satisfies. Then evaluate beneficial Long Rest eligibility. If eligible, apply its sourced benefits, including serum reset and one eligible expedition point when secure. Persistent food/water/source blocks still prevent expedition reduction. An additional safe RestWatch inside the24h reward cap can discharge debt but cannot restore resources, remove expedition Strain, reset the beneficial-rest clock or reset short-rest counts.

**Secure Long Rest.** Remove one eligible expedition point chosen by the patient, once the rest qualifies and no reduction block remains. This is a separate benefit from serum reset, so one actual qualifying rest may do both. Class-only serum reduction never silently removes expedition points.

**Morale Rest — NEW endpoint.** Four consecutive safe hours of voluntarily chosen recreation, without forced substance use, work, expedition travel or simultaneous sleep/ShortRest. At most one beneficial Morale Rest per24 elapsed hours. Remove one eligible expedition point. It never removes a Wound. A distinct4hMoraleRest plus an eligible8hsecureLongRest can legitimately remove two points; there is no new shared one-point cap.

**Haven care.** One full day means24 consecutive hours under qualifying Haven care/location conditions, with real care, food and water supplied under campaign rules. One active care interval per patient; interrupted care gives no completion benefit and restarting requires a fresh24h window. At completion remove all eligible ordinary expedition points; blocked/special points remain. The care window may contain separate sleep, meals and4h recreation because it is not24h of active practitioner work. Incompatible practitioner activities cannot be double-counted.

The Strain reference does not replace HP/RP/RC rest rewards or settle all supply prices, travel limits or camp security. Those systems retain their source review gates.

## Immunity, suppression and removal

Only explicit source-qualified wording changes a track. Poison immunity, global Exhaustion immunity, serum-profile tolerance and expedition immunity do not automatically cover serum Strain. Exhaustion removal does not clear either track. An unqualified future “immune to Strain” remains unbound.

- “Cannot gain expedition Strain” blocks gains only.
- “Ignore expedition Strain penalties” retains the points; no implied prevention of gain or level6 endpoint.
- “Remove X expedition Strain” actually removes eligible points under that source.

These tracks do not inherit the generic condition-immunity suppression rule merely because their UI label resembles a condition.

## Reference scope

The implementation in `tools/strain_playtest_rules.py` covers selected namespace lookups, gain/cap/death transitions, point recovery, numeric composition, Dash deadlines and completed-rest accounting. It does not run the campaign, grant class abilities, create inventory, verify all care activities, dispatch conditions or perform resurrection. The caller supplies legality and source eligibility. Its penalty projection does not replace independent life-state, collapse, condition or travel rules.

The namespace lookup rejects unknown/ambiguous sources. Low-level transition helpers such as `expedition_gain` accept already-validated source IDs from their caller; they do not independently repeat the registry lookup.

The [validation report](STRAIN_PLAYTEST_VALIDATION.json) records71 transition checks,30 exact source checks and4,949 maximum-HP invariant states. Broader rest rewards, travel, all-source class semantics, future Strain references, resurrection and human balance remain open.

# Time Loop: control and healing-pulse integration

**Bounded live control/pulse transaction interface jointly reviewed and reference-validated. Full Time Loop remains unavailable.**

The [actual nine-part conference](../../../../docs/audit/2026-10-08/full-game/GPT_TEMPORAL_CONTROL_PULSE_BOUNDARIES.md) supplements the [twelve world-conservation decisions](../../../../docs/audit/2026-10-08/full-game/GPT_TEMPORAL_WORLD_BOUNDARIES.md). The existing [control](CONTROL_STATES_PLAYTEST.md) and [pulse](HEALING_PULSE_PLAYTEST.md) guides continue to own ordinary source behavior. No original card was changed.

## Agreed temporal behavior

| State | Temporal rule |
| --- | --- |
| Explicit source/target regular endpoints | Restore remaining logical progress with authentic new-iteration regular markers. World elapsed time does not move backward, and restoration creates no marker event. |
| Current actual-turn endings | Remain attached to the actual application turn. The initiative-start snapshot has no active turn; a pending in-turn attachment there is invalid. Outside-turn +6-second endpoints retain their absolute deadline. |
| Outside-origin pulse schedules | Keep their original virtual markers and absolute deadlines. Entering initiative or using Time Loop does not restart them. Origin must be recorded explicitly. |
| Speed records | Same application, exact source/component/profile and valid endpoint. Do not reapply or refresh. Current external suppression remains authoritative. Aura, net, form, serum and creature children require their actual parent adapters. Hypermutation's floor is systemic parent state, not a hostile slow. |
| Guiding Bolt's Star mark | Restore its two separate entitlements. Keep the same mark identity and monotonic attack-token history; pending attacks block capture and preflight. |
| Wrathful Brand | Restore the separate owner/ally riders and snapshot timed parent. No new damage, healing or save event occurs at restore. |
| One-shot riders | Use exact parent/application/source/component identities and a finite trigger table. Vein Cutter consumes on its qualifying attack hit; Crippling Lash specifically requires a weapon hit. Omen Reader's once/encounter attack adjustment is distinct from the resulting timed star-ash. |
| Divine Judgment reflection | Retain historical actual-turn consumption. A genuinely new iteration turn can qualify, including a separately authenticated extra turn. Ordinary repeat saves and expiry still use regular markers. |
| PulseSeries | Restore snapshot pending/funded/consumed state under the same valid parent and fixed roster. No cast pulse or consumed-at-snapshot opportunity replays. A later pending paid pulse pays its current printed cost when actually due. |
| Recipient budgets | Retain history with domain, target and iteration-round identity. Circle of Harmony remains shared across owners in the same iteration-round. |
| Eternal Bloom | Preserve the original missing-HP capture and shares. Restore only snapshot installment availability; retain old consumption history. Do not grow the reserve from later damage. Its survival floor is separate. |
| First-contact cures | Restore snapshot instance/recipient entitlements. Garden uses entry/start; Enhanced Garden and Seed use their reviewed pulse event. Restore itself is none of these events. Real-rest recipient histories remain conserved. |
| Native healing | One evaluated opportunity at a genuine regular start during a real encounter. Decline, ineligibility or unavailable payment loses that start opportunity. Extra turns and downtime create no tick. A new iteration can supply a new genuine start, with current RP/reserves. |

**Resource-output conservation:** Transcendent Meditation's second pulse can supply1Ki only once for the same effect instance. Sacred Chant's third pulse can supply1Conviction only once for that instance. Reaching the occurrence while capped or while the whole effect is suppressed still consumes that resource opportunity. Healing may later replay under an authorized restored source without generating the same resource again. A never-reached opportunity remains eligible. Restoration itself grants neither resource.

For example, a Monk receives the second pulse's1Ki, then spends it. Rewinding to a snapshot where that pulse was pending can permit its healing again when legally due, but it cannot return that same1Ki. Sacred Chant uses the same conservation rule for Conviction.

The immutable snapshot is at initiative start. A source first created afterward is not silently added to that snapshot. An origin label cannot manufacture preexisting pulse state. Any logical-clock restoration must demonstrate that the actual source instance was already present in the captured state.

The conference's maintenance wording is read with its express instruction not to reopen ordinary mechanics: an early failed ordinary turn-window payment remains pending until the source's real turn-end deadline. Exact-due paid sequences/windows end immediately on failed upkeep. The notebook explicitly [confirmed this distinction and immutable snapshot membership](../../../../docs/audit/2026-10-08/full-game/GPT_TEMPORAL_PULSE_BRIDGE_CLOSURE.md). No currently supplied pulse profile needs a fabricated at-initiative creation exception; native passive abilities instead await their future genuine regular-start events.

## Current code and checks

`tools/temporal_control_playtest_rules.py` currently implements two limited bridges:

- `CanonicalPulseWallet` lets existing pulse helpers spend the real actor Wallet's RP/Bonus Action and the canonical Scheduler's RC. It owns no duplicate balances and rejects changed aliases before spending.
- `ConservedPulseOutputs` wraps actual `PulseSeries.resolve()` calls for the two resource-producing profiles. It retains unique occurrence IDs and conserved instance/index/component opportunities; it replaces the helper's raw Ki flag with the guarded allowance. Suppressed or capped resolved occurrences cannot be banked. Sacred Chant cannot generate Conviction outside a real encounter.

The returned resource allowance must be applied once by the host in the same atomic event, subject to the actual resource cap. These helpers do not themselves own, increment or restore Ki/Conviction. Source acquisition, legal recipients, actual parent concentration and authenticated due-event scheduling remain host/source-adapter responsibilities. The output guard cannot certify them.

[Validation](TEMPORAL_CONTROL_VALIDATION.json):22 focused methods pass. They exercise the actual existing maintenance, Song, Meditation, Chant and native payment interfaces, plus duplicate output, cap, suppression, early/duplicate occurrence and canonical-alias cases. A replay test deliberately resets only an isolated series view; it demonstrates the output guard, not a complete Time Loop source restoration. The [actual independent review](../../../../docs/audit/2026-10-08/full-game/GPT_TEMPORAL_PULSE_BRIDGE_CLOSURE.md) approves only these payment/resolved-output bridges. The [review manifest](TEMPORAL_PULSE_BRIDGE_REVIEW_STATUS.json) binds that approval to the exact unchanged helper. The validation JSON retains its original submitted pre-review scope label as evidence; the separate review manifest records the later disposition.

## Still required

The `tools/temporal_control_world.py` integration passes 50 methods, alongside the 76 foundation and 22 payment/output methods. The [actual notebook closure](../../../../docs/audit/2026-10-08/full-game/GPT_TEMPORAL_CONTROL_WORLD_CLOSURE.md) confirms the bounded interface after four review rounds. Its [review manifest](TEMPORAL_CONTROL_WORLD_REVIEW_STATUS.json) binds the exact helper, tests and foundation extension; it does not transfer this approval to future edits. It restores selected same-object fields, watches aliases and current concentration callbacks, preserves original outside-origin pulse clocks, and uses authenticated regular-start phases. Hemostasis uses the target's start; other admitted sequences use the source's. Bloom installments and pulse-triggered contacts require current parent occurrence receipts. Native optional healing records an evaluated start even when declined, ineligible or unaffordable.

The repaired world requires the host's existing `ConservedPulseOutputs` guard as an explicit constructor argument. It delegates resource-producing pulses to that same guard and watches its canonical bindings, consumption and event history in the restore transaction. There is no second independent-output ledger. Child operations reject a parent whose clock projection reveals missed upkeep. Capture rejects participant recipient-round claims until a real outside-round import adapter exists. Unclassified Speed suppression blocks capture/restore. Prepared plans also watch the concentration object's complete schema. Eternal Bloom and Crown Restored require concentration through the existing `oracle.engine[26]` zone rule; prepaid Final pulses do not waive that requirement.

Capture now checks that an active pulse already existed and remains live at the actual snapshot marker, without mutating it. Every pulse, installment, contact and native component has an exact admitted identifier. The adapter validates mutable collection types before resource/occurrence writes. When original outside-clock Bloom opportunities are already past, their shares are lost without healing; the installment cursor advances past them so a later authentic due installment can still resolve. No original missing-HP reserve or share is recomputed.

Snapshot concentration bindings include the actual owner, concentration ID, slot object and callback object. Retained references prevent identity-token reuse. A same-ID replacement, even with the same callback or subsequently registered components, rejects before writes. This preserves the original later-ending callback; it does not restore ended/replaced concentration.

This is still bounded component code. Exact supplied source/target schedules and source eligibility remain host inputs; original outside-initiative round-ledger import is not implemented. The new integration does not execute complete cards or apply HP/Ki/Conviction output to final life/resource holders. It admits only the explicit control policy rows and three paid native sources. Omen Reader, extra turns, movement/entry receipts, mutation reserves, shared multi-parent contact holders, device/stasis/copy parents and complete source sibling lifecycles remain unsupported. Missing or ended required concentration rejects restoration. Parent retirement/restoration beyond the existing exact callback is not implemented.

Complete nine-family/source restoration remains in progress. No supported-adapter count or ordinary catalog status has been promoted. Required work includes complete source clock/parent adapters, final resource/output application, complete shared recipient history across initiative boundaries, and the outstanding lifecycles above. [Validation](TEMPORAL_CONTROL_WORLD_VALIDATION.json) and the bounded approval do not certify full Time Loop.

Rapid Coagulation additionally needs the canonical previous-turn movement baseline from the initiative snapshot. It remains unsupported until that state exists. Net Bolt, Totem/Echo, Nano-Aegis, auras and other dependent sources remain unavailable to Time Loop without their physical/device/parent adapters. The seven major integrations and final whole-game/GitHub gate remain open.
